items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’m trying to think who it would be. King George and Queen Mary, I think. I go back that far.

ctx.x: At that point. Yeah, so . . . also that gives you an idea of the kind of environment that cultivated your interest in music. You told me about some of your family members that played also. Were there music that you heard in the community? Were there other neighbors? Were there pianos in the homes of others?

No, not really, not really. I do remember going down to visit my uncle Harry, one of the . . . Mummy’s uncles in Windsor. I remember that very fondly. That again was an early musical experience, probably very close after starting on the piano at home that Mummy played. And this Uncle Harry and Aunt Francis—I remember them very well. I guess they were quite elderly at the time. Anyway, I loved Uncle Harry. I thought he was a very sweet guy. They had this little upright piano that was . . . I wasn’t smart enough to…
Is this the Queen Mother you’re referring to?
